title: Fried Dough Dough
source: Chef Jamie Roraback, NBC Connecticut (Country Fair Fried Dough), adapted

items.body: In the large bowl, stir the yeast and sugar into the lukewarm water until dissolved. Stir in the olive oil.
Add the flour and salt to the water. Stir with a spatula until no dry flour is left. It will be a sticky, shaggy ball. Cover and rest 15 min.

With a wet hand, pull an edge of the dough up and fold it into the middle; turn the bowl and repeat all the way around, ≈30 s. Cover. Repeat every 15 min, 3 rounds in all. Then rub a little olive oil over it, cover, and let rise until doubled, 30–45 min.

Brush the sheet pan with olive oil. Turn the dough onto the counter, divide it into 10 pieces with the bench scraper (≈88 g each), and roll each into a ball. Set them on the pan a few inches apart, oil the tops lightly, cover loosely, and let rise until puffy, ≈25 min. Heat the frying oil now.
Gently stretch each ball into a ≈8 in round, thinner in the middle; a lopsided shape is fine. If it springs back, let it rest 5 min and stretch again. Fry and top as on the Grammy’s Fried Dough card.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: Branded Foods labels (King Arthur All-Purpose, Morton) and SR Legacy (yeast, counted as active dry; sugar; olive oil). Per piece, before frying: frying oil and toppings not counted. Water and the oil for the dough and pan not counted.
notes: Make ahead: refrigerate the covered balls up to 1½ days; let them soften at room temp, ≈30–60 min (our estimate). One batch ≈ 2 Rhodes loaves.
Flour is her 3½ cups plus the ½ cup she adds if sticky; 3½ cups at 120 g would be too wet to stretch. Folds replace her 5 min knead. She fries at 375 °F (191 °C), ≈1 min a side, to deep golden.
